question: Bank of Russia decision in September?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the change in the key rate resulting from the Bank of Russia’s September meeting, relative to the level it was prior to this meeting.

The resolution source for this market is information released by the Bank of Russia after its September 11, 2026 meeting as listed on the official Bank of Russia calendar: https://www.cbr.ru/eng/dkp/cal_mp/#t13

This market may resolve as soon as the Bank of Russia’s press release for their September 11, 2026 meeting with relevant data is issued. If no decision on the key rate is issued by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, this market will resolve to the "No change" bracket.
research:
I found nothing published on or before 2026-09-06 that settles the question. Before the meeting, opinion was split between a hold at 14% and a 25 bp cut to 13.75%, and few expected a hike. Sources dated after 2026-09-06 were excluded.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-09-06: The Bank of Russia's calendar lists 2026 key rate meetings on 13 Feb, 20 Mar, 24 Apr, 19 Jun, 24 Jul, **11 Sep**, 23 Oct and 18 Dec. [CBR calendar](https://www.cbr.ru/eng/dkp/cal_mp/)
- 2026-07-24: The latest decision before the meeting cut the key rate 25 bp, from 14.25% to **14.00%**, effective 27 July. This 14.00% is the reference level for the question. [TASS](https://tass.com/economy/2164709); [Meduza](https://meduza.io/en/news/2026/07/24/russia-s-central-bank-cuts-key-rate-for-10th-time-in-a-row-to-14)

## 2. Current status
- Nothing published by 2026-09-06 settles the outcome. The decision is due 11 September, and the press release usually comes out at 13:30 Moscow time (10:30 UTC).

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-03: Sberbank's CFO put the odds of another 25 bp cut versus a pause at roughly 50/50, according to an Interfax headline. [Interfax](https://www.interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/?tag=Expectations)
- 2026-09-02: At the Eastern Economic Forum, Anatoly Aksakov (head of the Duma financial markets committee) said he expects a **hold at 14%** because of pro-inflation risks. "With a small dose of optimism" he allowed for a 25 bp cut. The same article says Governor Nabiullina reported that in July the board discussed a 25 bp cut, a hold at 14.25%, and, according to some proposals, a **hike**. [Finance Mail](https://finance.mail.ru/article/aksakov-dopustil-chto-cb-ne-budet-snizhat-stavku-11-sentyabrya-69225678/)
- 2026-09-01: Analysts split:
  - Vladimir Chernov (Finance Global): a cut to 13.75% at about 55%, a hold at about 40%, a hike at no more than 5%.
  - Alexander Ivanov (Ingosstrakh-Investments): expects a pause.
  - Vladimir Bragin (Alfa-Capital): a sharp ruble fall or cost-driven inflation could push the central bank toward a hike.

  [Finance Mail](https://finance.mail.ru/article/cb-vstal-na-raspute-po-klyuchevoj-stavke-69225326/)
- Late August / early September: Weekly Rosstat data showed slight deflation in August, about -0.08% for the month. Annual inflation was about **6.32-6.33%** at end-August, the highest since November 2025. [AK&M](https://www.akm.ru/eng/news/deflation-in-the-russian-federation-for-the-week-was-0-01/); [Interfax](https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/118697/)
- August 2026: A central bank survey showed household inflation expectations easing to 13.7%, back to the January level. [Interfax](https://www.interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/?tag=Expectations)
- 2026-08-05: The central bank published the summary of its July discussion. Excerpts say household and business price expectations "rose significantly" in July, and professional analysts raised their inflation forecasts for 2026-2028. I could not load the full PDF, so I can't report the board's discussion of options. [CBR summary PDF](https://www.cbr.ru/Content/Document/File/194289/summary_key_rate_05082026.pdf)
- 2026-07-24: Key points of the July decision:
  - Most analysts had expected a hold, so the cut was a surprise.
  - The central bank raised its 2026 inflation forecast to 6-7% and lowered its GDP forecast to 0-1%.
  - It set the average key rate forecast for 2026 at 14.5-14.6%, which implies little easing for the rest of the year.
  - It signalled a "more gradual" pace of cuts.
  - Nabiullina linked the rise in expectations to the fuel market.

  [intellinews](https://www.intellinews.com/russia-s-central-bank-cuts-rate-to-14-in-surprise-move-lifts-inflation-forecast-to-6-7-456776/); [opovo](https://www.opovo.com.br/noticias/economia/2026/07/24/bc-da-russia-corta-juros-em-25-pontos-base-a-14-e-indica-reducao-gradual-a-frente.html); [Finance Mail](https://finance.mail.ru/article/cb-vstal-na-raspute-po-klyuchevoj-stavke-69225326/)

## 4. Base rates
- The July cut was the **10th straight cut**. The rate has fallen from 21% in mid-2025 to 14%, with the last several steps at 25 bp (for example 14.5% to 14.25% on 19 June, then 14.25% to 14% on 24 July). Every meeting from June 2025 to July 2026 ended in a cut. [Meduza](https://meduza.io/en/news/2026/07/24/russia-s-central-bank-cuts-key-rate-for-10th-time-in-a-row-to-14); [Finance Mail](https://finance.mail.ru/article/aksakov-dopustil-chto-cb-ne-budet-snizhat-stavku-11-sentyabrya-69225678/)
- The central bank's own average-rate path (14.5-14.6% for 2026) leaves room for only a little further easing. That fits pauses alternating with small cuts.
- In past episodes, such as 2020, the central bank paused when inflation picked up during an easing cycle. [Bloomberg 2020](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-09-18/russia-hits-brakes-on-monetary-easing-as-inflation-accelerates)

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has a market called "Bank of Russia decision in September?" with outcomes Decrease, No Change and Increase. Snapshots on aggregator sites disagree and are thinly traded:
  - A page updated 2026-07-24 showed No Change at about 74%.
  - Another snapshot showed No Change at about 50% and Decrease at about 41%.

  I could not get a reliable price dated close to 2026-09-06. [predscope](https://predscope.com/event/bank-of-russia-decision-in-september-20260623013858993); [polymarkets mirror](https://polymarkets.co.il/en/market/bank-of-russia-decision-in-september-20260623013858993/)
- Kalshi lists a related market (KXCBDECISIONRUSSIA-26SEP11). I could not retrieve its price. [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxcbdecisionrussia/russia/kxcbdecisionrussia-26sep11)
- Experts as of early September: roughly evenly split between a hold and a 25 bp cut, with hike odds put at about 5% or less (Chernov, Aksakov, Sberbank's CFO, Ivanov; sources in section 3).
- I did not find a Reuters poll for the September meeting dated before 2026-09-06.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-09-09: Rosstat's weekly CPI for 1-8 September, plus the Economy Ministry's annual inflation estimate.
- Ruble moves and fuel-market news, including any diesel or gasoline export curbs and price spikes.
- Any official comments before the quiet period.
- 2026-09-11: The board decision and press release, followed by Nabiullina's press conference.

- 5 August: The summary of the July discussion said household and business price expectations "rose significantly."
- End of August: Annual inflation was about 6.3%, the highest since November 2025. August itself showed slight deflation (about -0.08%), and household inflation expectations eased to 13.7%.
- 1-3 September: Opinion was split.
  - Chernov: 55% cut, 40% hold, 5% or less hike.
  - Aksakov and Ivanov: expect a hold.
  - Sberbank's CFO: roughly 50/50.
  - Nabiullina said a hike was among the proposals discussed in July.
- Polymarket snapshots were thin, at roughly 50% No Change and 41% Decrease.

(e) **Unexpected scenarios:**
- A sharp ruble slide or a fuel-price spike in early September could push the board to a hike.
- A benign weekly CPI print plus weak GDP data could lead to a larger 50 bp cut. That would still resolve as "Decrease."

**Adjustment:** I started from the market's split of about 50% hold and 41% cut. I moved a few points toward a hold because of the bank's own rate path, rising annual inflation and the "more gradual" signal. The July surprise cut shows this board is willing to ease against consensus, so I kept substantial weight on a cut. I put 5% on a hike for tail risk.
